adversarialCases.scenario: A live-but-quiet client (non-heartbeat frames only) is never reaped, even with many sweeps.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: Leases are granted ONLY for client_heartbeat frames. Control/query/event_replay/session_activate/unknown frames from chat clients across 12 sweeps (60s fake time) never grant a lease; onClientLivenessEmpty never fires; host stays started.

adversarialCases.scenario: Disconnect + reconnect heartbeat within TTL keeps the host alive; only after TTL elapses does onClientLivenessEmpty fire exactly once.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: handleDisconnect does NOT delete the lease; a reconnect heartbeat at 5s refreshes it; sweep at 15s keeps the host alive; at 20s the lease expires and empty fires exactly once (later sweeps at 25s/30s/60s do not re-fire).

adversarialCases.scenario: TTL boundary precision: lease reaped at exactly now - heartbeatAt >= 15000.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: Sweep at 14999ms keeps the lease; sweep at 15000ms reaps it and fires empty.

adversarialCases.scenario: Two concurrent heartbeat clients: host notifies empty only after BOTH leases expire (staggered re-heartbeat).
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: Client b re-heartbeats at 5s; at 15s only a's lease is stale (empty stays 0); at 20s b's lease is stale too and empty fires once.

adversarialCases.scenario: The last client to re-heartbeat determines when empty fires (re-heartbeat overtakes the other client's expiry).
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: a re-heartbeats at 19s; b reaped at 20s (empty 0, a alive); a reaped at 34s and only then empty fires.

adversarialCases.scenario: A client that stops heartbeating mid-session (socket stays open, other frames keep flowing) is reaped after TTL.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: control_request at 10s and event_replay at 14.5s do NOT refresh the lease; sweep at 15s reaps it and fires empty.

adversarialCases.scenario: Start/stop/restart cycle: second start resets lease state so the once-only notify can fire again on the next cycle.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: Cycle 1: heartbeat -> sweep reaps -> empty fires once; stop clears the timer. Cycle 2: start clears leases and re-arms the once-only flag; heartbeat -> sweep -> empty fires again (count 2); stop clears the re-armed timer.

adversarialCases.scenario: Startup failure (registration rejection) clears the sweep timer (no leaked interval).
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: start() rejects; host.started false; the armed timer handle is cleared exactly once (clearedHandles == armedHandles); a retried start re-arms the timer and succeeds.

adversarialCases.scenario: Stop rollback: a failing unregister keeps the host started with the timer armed.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: stop() rejects; host.started stays true; clearInterval NOT called (timer armed); the sweep keeps running; a retry with a healthy unregister succeeds, clears the timer, and unregister is attempted exactly twice.

adversarialCases.scenario: bridge-client clientHeartbeatMs: frame emission, restart on reconnect, stop-after-close.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: Immediate heartbeat on connect plus interval-driven beats (real 25ms interval); after the socket dies and the client reconnects on demand, ONLY the new socket keeps heartbeating (old socket's frame count frozen), and close() halts emission on the live socket.

adversarialCases.scenario: A fresh heartbeat after empty re-arms liveness; notify fires again once the new lease expires.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: After empty fires at 15s, a heartbeat at 16s grants a new lease (once-only flag reset by #heartbeatClient); at 30s still alive; at 31s the new lease expires and notify fires again (count 2).

adversarialCases.scenario: A host that never sees a heartbeat never fires empty and keeps its timer armed.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: 10 sweeps with an empty lease table: no notify (guarded on #hasClientLease), host stays started, timer stays armed until stop().

adversarialCases.scenario: A heartbeat whose connectionId does not match the transport grants no lease and yields an error frame.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: requireConnection rejects the spoofed frame; a reverse_response ok:false error frame is sent; no lease exists, so a 60s sweep never fires empty.

adversarialCases.scenario: A throwing onClientLivenessEmpty propagates through the sweep but fires only once per lease generation.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The notify call has no try/catch: the throw surfaces from the sweep callback; the once-only flag is set before the call so later sweeps do not re-invoke it; a fresh heartbeat re-arms and the next expiry invokes (and throws) again.

adversarialCases.scenario: clientHeartbeatMs is not floored: 0 runs the heartbeat interval at timer minimum.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: Observed: with clientHeartbeatMs: 0 the client emitted >20 heartbeat frames in a 150ms window (Bun clamps the delay to ~1ms). No validation/floor exists on the option. Not part of the PR's contract (ACP_SESSION_RECONNECT uses 5000) — API hardening gap only.

observations: T7 rollback: while a stop is stuck on a failing unregister, #stopping stays true, so a sweep that empties the lease table cannot fire the notify; the host only tears down once a stop retry succeeds. Matches the PR's stated rollback contract (host stays started, timer armed) but means an orphaned host with persistent unregister failure will not self-shutdown.

A13: #notifyClientLivenessEmpty has no try/catch — a synchronously throwing onClientLivenessEmpty propagates out of the sweep interval callback (in production: surfaces from a setInterval callback). The once-only flag is set before the call, so it still fires once per lease generation. The runtime wiring passes () => ctx.shutdown(), which returns a promise and is unlikely to throw synchronously.

OBS-C: SdkClientOptions.clientHeartbeatMs has no floor or validation; 0/negative values run the interval at the timer minimum (~1ms). The wired constant ACP_SESSION_RECONNECT.clientHeartbeatMs is 5000, so the shipped path is unaffected.

Coverage: no test outside packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-host.test.ts exercises onClientLivenessEmpty; the session-runtime.ts wiring (onClientLivenessEmpty: () => ctx.shutdown()) is type-checked only. Verified by grep across packages/coding-agent.

bridge-client reconnect is demand-driven: an active-socket death does not auto-create a new open cycle; the client reconnects on the next connect()/request. Heartbeat restart on the new incarnation is correct: the old interval is cleared in #retire and again in #startHeartbeat, and the isActive guard prevents stale-socket sends.
